submissions.title: AWS proceeds with data center project in Walla Walla, Washington
submissions.excerpt: The campus is expected to have a 300MW power capacity
submissions.suggestedProjectName: AWS Attalia Data Center Campus (Walla Walla County, Washington)
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT, NOT YET APPROVED — flagging as a pending signal, not a settled announcement. AWS/Amazon Data Services scaled back its Wallula Gap-area plan to a ~300MW, 3-building 'Attalia' campus on 134 of the 554 acres bought from the Port of Walla Walla in Feb 2026 ($36M land deal); would be Amazon's first data center in Washington State (earlier plan was a $4.8B, 16-building campus in four phases). The county has NOT approved it — a SEPA environmental review is in progress, with a second public-comment period still to come. Of 706 comments in a 30-day period ending Oct 12, 2026, only ~23 (~3%) supported the project per a Walla Walla Union-Bulletin tally — strong local opposition. Treat the 300MW figure as site-power-basis from county planning documents, not an AWS-confirmed IT load figure. CAUTION: datacenterdynamics.com was not reachable from this sandbox (WebFetch blocked) — the excerpt is reconstructed from a search-engine summary, not independently re-opened. Recommend the reviewer hold this one for county approval or a direct Amazon statement.

claims.methodology: Walla Walla County planning documents (cited via DCD) give a 300MW capacity for the proposed campus, which is still under SEPA review and not yet approved; basis (site power vs IT load) is unstated in reporting.
